eyebrow: checkout gets its own network and database
code:
$ docker network create northbridge-checkout-net

$ docker run -d --name checkout-db \
  --network northbridge-checkout-net \
  -v checkout-db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data \
  -e POSTGRES_DB=checkout \
  postgres:16
caption: Same shape as catalog-db in the last lesson -- named volume for persistence, user-defined network for DNS.

eyebrow: A hostname, not an IP, in the config file
caption: checkout-db:5432 -- the container's actual name, not an address anyone has to update by hand.

eyebrow: Starting checkout on the same network
code:
$ docker run -d --name checkout \
  --network northbridge-checkout-net \
  --env-file checkout.env \
  northbridge/checkout:2.1

$ docker logs checkout
Connecting to database at checkout-db:5432...
Connected to checkout-db:5432 (PostgreSQL 16.2)
caption: Nothing in checkout's config needed an IP -- Docker's embedded DNS resolved checkout-db the moment the app asked for it.
